implication: The 31(4) disclosure is a procedural gating item in Indian M&A: any acquirer crossing 25% or entering into an open offer must file within two trading days; failure to file or disclosure breaches expose the acquirer to SEBI enforcement action and potential trading bans.

headline: Ramesh D. Poddar files substantial acquisition disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Ramesh D. Poddar has filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. The filing signals a material change in shareholding or control interest in Siyaram Silk Mills Limited, triggering mandatory disclosure obligations.
detail: Ramesh D. Poddar submitted a formal disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI Takeover Code, which requires parties effecting substantial acquisitions (crossing the 25% threshold or entering into an open offer) to disclose within two trading days. The filing was made to NSE and is publicly available on the exchange's corporate action archive. This disclosure does not specify the quantum of shares acquired, the consideration, or the intent (voluntary vs. open offer), but its filing confirms that a threshold event has occurred under the Takeover Code.
